t0.text: 00 · Motion: everything grows out of a pill

howto.text:
How to view

Row 00 shows every animation as a loop at half speed, each with a timeline and an orange playhead.

Rows 01–05: key hints are hidden. Press Play on an artboard and click anywhere on it to show or hide them, or flip showKeys in its Tweaks.

Read the two purple notes on the far left first: global interaction rules and the animation system. Each row has a flow note on its left; each artboard has a note on its right.

anim.text:
Animation system

One material, one set of curves. Durations are for real use; the boards play at half speed.

Sizes
• Micro (hover, press, toggle, colour change): 120 ms, OutCubic
• Small (popovers, tooltips, OSD fill, title cross-fade): 180–220 ms
• Medium (launcher, Control Center, notification center, sheets): 320–420 ms, OutBack 1.15 opening, InCubic closing
• Large (lock, log in, wallpaper ripple, overview zoom): 450–700 ms, InOutCubic
• Closing always takes about 60 % of the opening time.

Patterns
• Grow from the pill: a droplet the size of the pill stretches, a short neck forms, then it springs into the panel. Content fades up 6–10 px once the shape is 60 % done.
• Split / merge: temporary pills bud off the clock (recording, sharing, key modes) and merge back into it.
• Rise: full-screen overlays dim first (200 ms), then rise or scale in from 92 %.
• Shake: errors shake sideways 4 times with damping (300 ms). Sideways means "no".
• Stagger: groups of tiles or rows arrive 30–40 ms apart.

Liquid Glass details
• The specular top edge brightens on hover and follows the cursor.
• While a panel moves, its blur is lowered and comes back when it settles, so motion stays smooth on battery.

Reduced motion (config flag): every grow / split becomes a 150 ms fade, no overshoot, no shake (the field just turns red).

rules.text:
Global interaction rules

One thing at a time
• Only one panel is open at once (launcher, Control Center, notification center, wallpaper switcher, cheatsheet, overview, power menu). Opening another merges the old one back into its pill while the new one grows out of its own.
• Esc closes the topmost thing; a click outside closes too. Focus returns to the window you were in.
• Popovers (media, workspace peek, menus) close when a panel opens.

Layers, top to bottom
1. Lock screen
2. Password prompts (polkit, SSH/GPG), centred on a dim layer
3. Capture tool
4. Power menu
5. Panels and popovers
6. Toasts and OSDs
7. Pills
8. Windows

How things affect each other
• Locking closes every panel and cancels open password prompts.
• Capture hides toasts, OSDs and its own UI from the image; a recording also hides the red pill.
• OSDs don't show while Control Center is open (its sliders already move).
• While the notification center is open, new notifications go straight into the list.
• Fullscreen, game mode and do not disturb hold toasts back and summarise them afterwards; critical ones always show.
• Fullscreen hides the pills; switching window or workspace brings them back.
• The power button in Control Center morphs the panel into the power menu.
• While a password prompt is up, Super shortcuts are ignored except Esc.
• Changing the wallpaper recolours everything at once: pills, panels, borders, kitty, GTK, Qt, greeter.

Mouse
• Left click opens, right-click gives options, scroll changes the value under the cursor (workspace on the workspace pill, track on the media pill, volume on the status pill).
• Hover is never required: everything that reacts to hover also has a click or key.

Keyboard
• Super + letter opens, Super+Shift + letter captures, Esc closes.
• Inside surfaces: arrows or H J K L, Enter, Tab, Alt+1–9.
• Hold Alt in any open surface to show its key hints.

intro.text:
Glass Shell: concept sketches (v4)

The bar is five separate glass pills that hug their content: workspaces + focused window, a compact media pill (only while something plays), clock, status and bell. Every panel grows out of the pill it belongs to.

What's new in v4
• Login and lock redesigned: thicker Outfit clock, picture + name above a lower password pill, user switcher (login), power options (both).
• Every popup and state: pill popovers, launcher states, Control Center sub-pages, notification states, annotate, colour picker, countdown, share picker, session edge cases.
• Animations for everything in row 00.

Look
Dark, matugen colours from the wallpaper (shown: Dusk). Glass strength lives in the Quickshell config file (Balanced shown). Clock face on greeter and lock: Outfit SemiBold; everything else Geist.

flow-launcher.text:
Launcher family: flow

• Super+Space opens Apps. Typing a prefix switches mode in place (= ; : > / ? !); Backspace on an empty field goes back to Apps.
• Super+V, Super+. and Super+Shift+Space open straight into Clipboard, Emoji and Shortcuts.
• Tab cycles modes; the chip row follows.
• Enter acts and closes. Shift+Enter is the alternative (paste instead of copy, run in kitty, private window).
• Esc closes; the sheet merges back into the clock pill.
• Nothing is remembered between opens except history (calculator, commands, clipboard, recent apps).

flow-panels.text:
Panels: flow

• Control Center: Super+A or the status pill. Tiles toggle; › opens a sub-page; Esc goes back a page, then closes.
• Notification center: Super+N, the clock or the bell. J/K through the list, R reply, D dismiss, Enter opens the app (the center closes).
• Wallpaper: Super+W. Browsing previews the accents; Enter applies with the ripple; Esc reverts.
• Jumping between panels with their shortcuts (e.g. Super+A, then Super+N) merges one into its pill while the other grows out of its own.

flow-capture.text:
Capture: flow

1. Super+Shift+S: soft flash, freeze, dim; the toolbar rises. R / W / S picks the target, Tab switches photo ↔ video.
2. Photo: Enter → flash → copied + saved → thumbnail in the corner for 6 s (E annotate, S save as, X delete, click to open).
3. Video: Enter → optional countdown → red pill splits off the clock → Super+Shift+R or click the pill → toast with Copy / Open folder / Trim.
4. Colour: Super+Shift+C → click → hex copied, swatch in clipboard history.
5. When an app asks to share the screen, the share picker opens; while sharing, a green pill sits next to the clock.

flow-session.text:
Session: flow

• Boot → greeter → type password (Alt+U to switch user) → Enter → log-in animation → desktop.
• Super+L, idle, lid close or suspend → lock. Type → Enter → unlock.
• Idle chain: dim + 10 s countdown → lock at 5 min → screen off at 7 min → suspend at 15 min on battery (no suspend on AC). Skipped while video plays or Keep awake is on.
• Super+Esc → power menu on the desktop; Alt+P → power options on greeter and lock.
• Apps asking for admin rights → polkit dialog above everything except the lock screen. SSH/GPG passphrases use the same dialog.

n-mc.text:
Motion: status pill → Control Center

What: A glass droplet appears on top of the status pill, stretches down with a short liquid neck, then springs into the panel with a little overshoot. Closing reverses it without overshoot.

Why: The pill never moves, so your eye stays anchored. Seeing the panel come out of the thing you clicked makes the shell feel like one material.

Real timings: open ≈ 400 ms (OutBack), close ≈ 220 ms (InCubic), content fades in from 60 % of the shape.

n-ml.text:
Motion: clock → launcher, bell → toast

What: The launcher drips out of the clock pill and springs into the centre while the desktop dims. Later a Discord message widens the bell pill along the top edge, drops into a toast, drains its timer and gets pulled back into the bell, leaving a dot.

Why: Every surface has a home pill it comes from and returns to. That's what makes separate pills feel connected.

n-mp.text:
Motion: pill morphs

What: Four loops: switching workspace, the media pill appearing, the recording pill splitting off the clock, and an OSD dropping out of the clock.

Why: Pills never jump or pop. Every change is a shape change of the same glass, so you can follow it from the corner of your eye while coding or gaming.

Rule of thumb: what appears stretches out of its parent; what leaves merges back into it.

n-mo.text:
Motion: panels & overlays

What: Notification center, power menu, password prompt, capture, Control Center sub-pages and the toast stack.

Why: Panels that belong to a pill grow out of it. Full-screen overlays (power, polkit, capture) don't belong to a pill, so they dim the screen first and then rise or scale in at the centre. Errors always shake sideways, never up and down.

n-mw.text:
Motion: windows & workspaces

What: Window open and close, workspace slide, overview zoom, Alt+Tab and fullscreen. These are Hyprland's own animations, set in hyprland.lua to match the shell's curves.

Suggested values: windowsIn popin 86 % 280 ms · windowsOut popin 90 % 200 ms · workspaces slide 300 ms · fade 200 ms · one soft-spring bezier for all, e.g. (0.2, 0.9, 0.1, 1.05).

n-ms.text:
Motion: log in → lock → unlock → log out

What: One continuous loop.
• Log in: the password pill spins, avatar and field sink away, and the big clock shrinks and flies up until it is the clock pill. The other pills drop in from the top edge; windows fade in from 96 %.
• Lock (Super+L or idle): the reverse. Pills float up, the desktop blurs, the clock grows out of its pill to full size, avatar + field rise from below.
• Unlock: like logging in, but the windows were never gone, so only the blur clears.
• Log out / power off: fade to black.

Why: The clock is the one element on every screen, so it carries you between them. Greeter and lock share one layout, so both transitions feel the same.

n-mwall.text:
Motion: changing the wallpaper

What: Super+W raises the strip. Moving through it cross-fades only the accent colours (pills, borders, kitty), so you can preview without the screen flashing. Enter: the new wallpaper spreads out from the chosen thumbnail as a growing circle while the sheet sinks away. matugen, kitty, GTK and Qt reload in the background while the circle grows, so the colours have caught up when it covers the screen.

Esc while browsing cross-fades the accents back.

n-main.text:
Desktop: everyday tiling

What: Hyprland tiling with kitty, a browser and Discord, 10 px gaps, five floating glass pills on top.

Why: Separate islands use less space than one bar and let the wallpaper show between them. Each pill hugs its content (12–14 px around text, 6 px around round elements so they sit concentric in the 19 px radius) and only exists while it has something to show. Left: five workspace dots plus the focused window's icon and title. No tray icons: background apps live in Control Center.

Keys: Super+1–9 workspace · Super+H/J/K/L focus · Super+Q close · Super+F fullscreen · Super+T float · Super+Return terminal · Super+B browser

n-bar.text:
Pill states & OSDs

What: The pills in every state: default, empty workspace + nothing playing, recording, key mode (resize submap), low battery, do-not-disturb + game mode. Below: the workspace pill up close and the OSDs (volume, brightness, layout).

Why: Workspaces are five dots, no numbers: a wide accent capsule for where you are, filled dots for workspaces with windows, rings for empty ones, orange for urgent. Beside it, the focused app's icon + title. New information gets its own pill that splits off the clock (recording timer, resize mode). Warnings tint the pill they belong to.

Keys: media keys · Super+Shift+R stop recording · Super+R resize mode · Super+G game mode

n-popovers.text:
Pill popovers, menus & tooltips

What: Everything that opens from a pill without being a full panel:
• Workspace peek: hover a dot for 400 ms to see that workspace's windows; click to go there.
• Media: click the media pill. Cover, seek bar, controls, and a player switcher when several apps play.
• Tooltips: hover 600 ms, one line, only where an icon's state isn't obvious.
• Keyboard layout: left-click DE cycles, right-click lists layouts.
• Bell: right-click for do-not-disturb timers and clear all.
Below: the shared hover / press / open / focus / disabled states.

Why: Small questions get small answers right where you're pointing, without opening Control Center.

n-overview.text:
Overview & window switcher

What: Super+Tab zooms out to all workspaces with live previews. Alt+Tab is the quick most-recently-used switcher.

Why: The dots in the workspace pill tell you which workspaces are in use; this is the full map with previews when you need one. Typing filters windows by name.

Keys: Super+Tab · arrows or H/J/K/L · Enter focus · Shift+Enter move window here · Alt+Tab

n-launcher.text:
Launcher: apps

What: Super+Space drips a glass sheet out of the clock pill: search field, ranked results, mode chips.

Why: The first result is always pre-selected, so Super+Space, f, Enter launches Firefox in under a second. The chips show the prefixes, so you learn them by seeing them.

Keys: type to search · ↑↓ or Ctrl+J/K · Enter launch · Alt+1–9 jump · Tab next mode · Esc

n-lstates.text:
Launcher states

What: Just opened (recent apps + a couple of useful suggestions), no results (offers pacman install, web search, run in kitty), Files mode (/) and Command mode (>).

Why: The launcher should never be a dead end. An empty field shows what you probably want next; a failed search turns into the next sensible action.

Keys: ← → recents · Enter · Alt+1–9 · Ctrl+Enter open folder · Ctrl+C copy path · Shift+Enter run in kitty

n-modes.text:
Launcher modes

What: Same sheet, different prefix: = calculator, ; clipboard history, : emoji, > run command, / files.

Why: One shape for every 'find something' task instead of five separate tools. Clipboard history is a launcher mode (not a bar item), with a preview pane for images and code.

Keys: Super+V clipboard · Super+. emoji · type = for maths · Enter copies (Shift+Enter pastes) · Del removes an entry · P pins

n-cheat.text:
Shortcut cheatsheet

What: Super+Shift+Space: the same sheet as the launcher, listing every bind by category, searchable.

Why: It looks and moves like the launcher, so it feels like a search, not a manual. Binds are read from your hyprland.lua so it never goes stale. Here the keycaps are the content, so they always show; only the footer hints toggle.

Keys: type to filter · Tab next group · Enter run · Esc

n-control.text:
Control Center

What: Super+A (or a click on the status pill) drops a panel from the status pill: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, toggles, sliders, media, power profile, battery and background apps. The source pill stays tinted while it's open.

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth: clicking a tile toggles it; its › arrow (or Enter) opens one shared Wi-Fi & Bluetooth page, focused on the section you came from.

The round buttons at the top: sliders opens your Quickshell config in nvim; power morphs the panel into the power menu.

Keys: Super+A · 1–8 toggles · ←→ on a focused slider · Enter opens a sub-page

n-cpages.text:
Control Center sub-pages

What: Sound (output, input with live mic level, per-app volume), Wi-Fi password entry, Bluetooth pairing with a code, the background-app menu, and an expanded Night light tile.

Why: Everything stays inside the same panel. Sub-pages push in from the right; small extras (password, pairing code, night light) grow in place instead of opening a new window.

How you get there: › or Enter on a tile, a click on a slider's label, Enter or right-click on a background app.

n-notif.text:
Notifications & calendar

What: Toasts drop out of the bell pill. Super+N, or a click on the clock or bell, opens the center with calendar, today's events and grouped notifications.

Why: The calendar sits next to notifications because both answer 'what's going on'. Discord messages group per server with an inline reply field.

Keys: Super+N · J/K move · Enter open · R reply · D dismiss · Shift+D clear all · [ ] month · T today · Super+Shift+N do not disturb

n-nstates.text:
Notification states

What: Toast stack, critical toast, calendar reminder, inline reply, expanded group, progress card, empty center with do not disturb, catch-up summary, another day in the calendar.

Rules
• Max 3 toasts visible; the rest wait. Timers: 5 s, 10 s with actions, never for critical.
• Hovering a toast pauses its timer. Clicking opens the app and the toast merges back into the bell.
• While the center is open, new notifications go straight into the list.
• Do not disturb, fullscreen and game mode hold toasts back; afterwards you get one catch-up toast.
• Critical (battery 5 %, polkit denied, disk almost full) always shows.

n-wall.text:
Wallpaper switcher

What: Super+W shows a strip of wallpapers. Moving through it previews each matugen palette live on the pills, borders and kitty; Enter keeps it (ripple, see row 00), Esc reverts.

Why: One wallpaper = one theme, so choosing is purely visual. No options: glass strength and scheme live in the Quickshell config file.

Keys: Super+W · ←→ browse · Enter apply · R random · Esc revert

n-region.text:
Capture: region

What: Super+Shift+S freezes and dims the screen and shows a small toolbar: Region · Window · Screen, and Screenshot ↔ Record.

Why: One tool for every capture, so you never remember which script does what. A size readout, loupe and handles make precise crops. Afterwards a thumbnail waits in the corner: E opens Annotate, S save as, X delete.

Keys: Super+Shift+S · R / W / S pick target · Tab photo ↔ video · Enter capture · Esc cancel · Super+Shift+C colour picker

n-window.text:
Capture: window & recording

What: Window mode outlines the window under the cursor (Tab cycles). Recording options add microphone, desktop audio, cursor and format.

Why: Clipping a game moment or a bug demo should take two key presses. While recording, a red pill splits off the clock with a timer; click it or press the same bind to stop.

Keys: W window · Tab next window · M mic · A audio · D countdown · Enter start · Super+Shift+R stop

n-annotate.text:
Annotate

What: E on the screenshot thumbnail opens the image full screen with a toolbar: select, arrow, rectangle, pen, text, highlight, blur and crop; five colours (accent, red, yellow, white, black) and three stroke sizes.

Why: Most screenshots go to Discord or a bug report. Marking something and hiding a private tab shouldn't need GIMP.

Keys: V A R P T H B C tools · 1–5 colour · [ ] stroke · Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z · Del · Enter done (copies) · Ctrl+S save · Esc discard (asks once if there are edits)

n-cextras.text:
Colour picker, countdown, screen mode, recording done

What: The remaining capture surfaces: the colour picker (Super+Shift+C), the optional countdown before a recording, Screen mode, and what happens after a recording, including a simple trim strip.

Why: They all reuse the same toolbar, dim layer and accent frame, so capture always feels like one tool.

n-share.text:
Screen share picker

What: When Discord (or a browser) asks to share your screen, xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland calls this picker instead of its default one. Tabs: Screen, Window, Region; 1–9 pick a window; audio and 'remember' options at the bottom.

While sharing: a green pill splits off the clock, says what is being shared, and has a Stop button.

Why: You'll share your screen in Discord often; this makes it obvious what others can see.

Keys: Tab tabs · 1–9 or arrows pick · Enter share · Esc cancel

n-login.text:
Login (greetd + Quickshell greeter)

What: Wallpaper, a big clock in Outfit SemiBold, date, then lower down your profile picture, name and the coloured password pill. Bottom left: the user switcher chip (picture + name). Bottom right: battery and power.

Why: The clock is what you read from across the room; everything you interact with sits in the lower half, where your eyes go when you start typing. The user chip only appears when more than one user exists.

Profile picture: ~/.face (AccountsService). Without one: your initial on an accent-coloured circle.

Keys: type password · Enter · Alt+U users · Alt+P power

n-loginusers.text:
Login: user switcher

What: Alt+U or a click on the chip grows a list upward out of it. Each row: picture, name, last login. Moving the selection live-updates the big picture and name in the centre, and the field adapts (Guest: no password).

Keys: ↑↓ · Enter pick · Esc close

n-lock.text:
Lock screen

What: Same layout as the greeter over the blurred desktop: clock, date with a small lock, your picture, name and password pill. Bottom right: battery and power. No user switcher, no notifications, no media.

Why: Login and lock look identical, so there's one muscle memory. Just start typing; the field is always focused.

Keys: Super+L · type + Enter · Alt+P power

n-lockpower.text:
Lock / login: power options

What: Alt+P or a click on the power button grows a small menu upward: Suspend, Reboot, Power off. Log out isn't offered on the lock screen (that would skip the password). The greeter shows the same menu.

Confirm: Reboot and Power off arm on the first press: the row turns red with a 3 s ring. Press the same key or click again to confirm.

Keys: S suspend · R reboot · P power off · Esc close

n-sstates.text:
Session edge cases

What: Everything that can go wrong or wait around login, lock and authentication: wrong password, checking, Caps Lock, the idle countdown, a wrong polkit password, the armed power-off tile, critical battery, the shutdown screen, and SSH/GPG passphrase prompts.

n-polkit.text:
Password prompt (polkit)

What: A compact glass dialog over a dimmed screen whenever an app asks for admin rights.

Why: It names the requesting app and the exact action, so you can judge the request. Details reveal the polkit action ID. It always looks the same and appears only in this one spot, which makes fake prompts easier to spot.

Keys: type + Enter authenticate · Esc cancel · Tab details

n-power.text:
Power menu

What: Super+Esc: five large buttons over the dimmed desktop, nothing else.

Why: Each action has one letter (shown with the key hints), so Super+Esc, S suspends. Reboot and Power off arm on the first press (the tile turns red, see Session edge cases) and run on the second.

Keys: L lock · S suspend · O log out · R reboot · P power off · ←→ + Enter · Esc
